summary: Hugh Gray was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Battersea Grammar School, he served as a lecturer at the University of London and held a post at SOAS University of London around 1960.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate from Stanford University. He served as professor at Stony Brook University from 1974, executive director of the IAPL (~1976–2013), and held Fulbright Chairs in Vienna in 2000–2001 and 2009–2010.

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from EPHE in 2012 and studied under traditional teachers. He held a Newton International Fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of the EFEO in 2015.
Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada (~1968–1989) and held a post at Sophia University.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where she studied under MA supervisor Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He held posts at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1992), National Taiwan University of Arts (~1999–2014), and served as president of DILA (~2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under supervisor Guowei Liu, and also studied under teachers Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University for a Master of Arts degree under Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1991) and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University around 1992.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard (PhD ~1980–1987). He held posts at Harvard, Oxford, NYU, and became a distinguished service professor at the University of Chicago in 1994.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

Huston Smith was a scholar of religion and philosophy who studied at Central Methodist and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1940–1945). He held professorships at MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1990–1999).

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2010, under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under teacher Kapila Abhayawansa.
Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held posts as professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2026).
Hyacinth Bitschurin was a scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who was educated at Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique (~1826–1853).

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He held academic posts at Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences (~1957–1964), Aoyama Gakuin University (~1964–1994), and Open University of Japan (~1994–1999).

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and was a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara (attested 2015).

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1987–1989), and Harvard University (~1990–1992). He also trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).
